source_text: Πολλῆς οὖν οὔσης ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ζώοις τῆς φυσικῆς διαφορᾶς, καὶ αὐτῆς γε τῆς κατὰ φύσιν τροφῆς ἑκάστῳ γένει ζώου καὶ τῷ τρεφομένῳ σώματι συνεξαλλαττομένης, τριττῆς δὲ κατὰ τὴν ἑκάστου ζώου τροφὴν γινομένης καθάρσεως καὶ διακρίσεως, δεῖ πάντως φθείρεσθαι μὲν καὶ διαχωρεῖν ᾗ πέφυκεν ἢ πρὸς ἕτερόν τι μεταβάλλειν πᾶν ὁπόσον ἀλλότριον εἰς τὴν τοῦ ζώου τροφήν, ὡς συγκραθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενον, συμβαίνουσαν δὲ καὶ κατὰ φύσιν εἶναι τὴν τοῦ τρέφοντος σώματος δύναμιν ταῖς τοῦ τρεφομένου ζώου δυνάμεσι, καὶ ταύτην ἐλθοῦσαν δι᾿ ὧν πέφυκε κριτηρίων καὶ καθαρθεῖσαν ἀκριβῶς τοῖς φυσικοῖς καθαρσίοις εἰλικρινεστάτην γενέσθαι πρόσληψιν εἰς οὐσίαν· ἣν δὴ καὶ μόνην ἐπαληθεύων ἄν τις τοῖς πράγμασιν ὀνομάσειεν τροφήν, ὡς ἀποβάλλουσαν πᾶν ὁπόσον ἀλλότριον καὶ βλαβερὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ τρεφομένου ζώου σύστασιν καὶ τὸν πολὺν ἐκεῖνον ὄγκον ἐπεισαχθέντα πρὸς τὴν τῆς γαστρὸς ἀποπλήρωσιν καὶ τὴν τῆς ὀρέξεως θεραπείαν. Ἀλλὰ ταύτην μὲν οὐκ ἄν τις ἀμφισβητήσειεν ἑνοῦσθαι τῷ τρεφομένῳ σώματι, συνδιαπλεκομένην τε καὶ περιπλαττομένην πᾶσι τοῖς τούτου μέρεσι καὶ μορίοις· τὴν δὲ ἑτέρως ἔχουσαν καὶ παρὰ φύσιν φθείρεσθαι μὲν ταχέως, ἢν ἐῤῥωμενεστέρᾳ συμμίξῃ δυνάμει, φθείρειν δὲ σὺν εὐμαρείᾳ τὴν κρατηθεῖσαν, εἴς τε μοχθηροὺς ἐκτρέπεσθαι χυμοὺς καὶ φαρμακώδεις ποιότητας, ὡς μηδὲν οἰκεῖον ἢ φίλον τῷ τρεφομένῳ σώματι φέρουσαν. Καὶ τούτου τεκμήριον μέγιστον τὸ πολλοῖς τῶν τρεφομένων ζώων ἐκ τούτων ἐπακολουθεῖν ἄλγος ἢ κίνδυνον ἢ θάνατον, ἢν ὑπὸ σφοδροτέρας ὀρέξεως τῇ τροφῇ καταμεμιγμένον συνεφελκύσηταί τι φαρμακῶδες καὶ παρὰ φύσιν· ὃ δὴ καὶ πάντως φθαρτικὸν ἂν εἴη τοῦ τρεφομένου σώματος, εἴ γε τρέφεται μὲν τὰ τρεφόμενα τοῖς οἰκείοις καὶ κατὰ φύσιν, φθείρεται δὲ τοῖς ἐναντίοις. Εἴπερ οὖν τῇ διαφορᾷ τῶν τῇ φύσει διαφερόντων ζώων ἡ κατὰ φύσιν συνδιῄρηται τροφή, καὶ ταύτης γε αὐτῆς οὔτε πᾶν ὅπερ ἂν προσενέγκηται τὸ ζῶον οὔτε τὸ τυχὸν ἐκ τούτου τὴν πρὸς τὸ τρεφόμενον σῶμα δέχεται σύγκρασιν, ἀλλ᾿ αὐτὸ μόνον τὸ διὰ πάσης πέψεως κεκαθαρμένον καὶ μεταβεβληκὸς εἰλικρινῶς πρὸς τὴν τοῦ ποιοῦ σώματος ἕνωσιν καὶ τοῖς τρεφομένοις μέρεσιν εὐάρμοστον, εὔδηλον ὡς οὐδὲν τῶν παρὰ φύσιν ἑνωθείη ποτ᾿ ἂν τούτοις οἷς οὐκ ἔστι τροφὴ προσφυὴς καὶ κατάλληλος, ἀλλ᾿ ἤτοι κατ᾿ αὐτὴν τὴν κοιλίαν διαχωρεῖ, πρὶν ἕτερόν τινα γεννῆσαι χυμόν, ὠμὸν καὶ διεφθαρμένον, ἢ συστὰν ἐπὶ πλεῖον τίκτει πάθος ἢ νόσον δυσίατον, συνδιαφθείρουσαν καὶ τὴν κατὰ φύσιν τροφὴν ἢ καὶ αὐτὴν τὴν τῆς τροφῆς δεομένην σάρκα. Ἀλλὰ κἂν ἀπωσθῇ ποτε, φαρμάκοις τισὶν ἢ σιτίοις βελτίοσιν ἢ ταῖς φυσικαῖς δυνάμεσι νικηθέν, μετ᾿ οὐκ ὀλίγης ἐξεῤῥύη τῆς βλάβης, ὡς μηδὲν φέρον τοῖς κατὰ φύσιν εἰρηνικὸν διὰ τὸ πρὸς τὴν φύσιν ἀσύγκρατον.
thought_title: Only what is truly food can unite to a body
orientation: Athenagoras is answering critics who say resurrection is impossible because bodies eaten by animals become part of those animals; he is now explaining that only what is truly proper food can be united to a body, while what is contrary to nature is expelled or destroys.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore there is much natural difference in all animals, and the food that is according to nature itself changes along with each kind of animal and with the body being nourished, and since a threefold cleansing and separation takes place according to the food of each animal, it is altogether necessary that everything that is foreign to the food of the animal be destroyed and pass out in the way it is naturally disposed, or change into something else, since it cannot be blended together; and that the power of the nourishing body be in accord with and according to nature with the powers of the animal being nourished; and that this power, having gone through the criteria through which it is naturally disposed to go and having been cleansed precisely by the natural cleansings, become a most pure addition to substance; which indeed alone someone would truly name food, as it casts off everything foreign and harmful to the constitution of the animal being nourished and that great bulk brought in for the filling of the stomach and the service of appetite. But no one would dispute that this food is united to the body being nourished, being interwoven with and molded around all its parts and members; but the food that is otherwise disposed and contrary to nature is destroyed quickly, if it is mixed with a stronger power, and destroys with ease the power that has been overcome, and turns aside into wicked humors and poisonous qualities, as bringing nothing proper or friendly to the body being nourished. And the greatest proof of this is that pain or danger or death follows for many of the animals being nourished from these things, if by a more violent appetite something poisonous and contrary to nature is dragged in mixed with the food; which indeed would be altogether destructive of the body being nourished, if indeed the things being nourished are nourished by things proper and according to nature, but are destroyed by the opposite things. If therefore the food according to nature has been divided along with the difference of the animals differing in nature, and of this food itself neither everything whatever the animal brings to itself nor the chance part from this receives the blending with the body being nourished, but only that which has been cleansed through every digestion and has changed purely toward the union with the body of a certain quality and is well fitted to the parts being nourished, it is quite clear that none of the things contrary to nature would ever be united to those things for which it is not food suitable and appropriate, but either it passes out in the stomach itself, before generating some other humor, raw and corrupted, or having remained longer it produces suffering or a disease hard to cure, destroying along with it also the food according to nature or even the very flesh that needs food. But even if it is ever expelled, having been overcome by certain drugs or better foods or the natural powers, it flows out with no small harm, as bringing nothing peaceful to the things according to nature because of its being unblended with nature.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'food' for τροφή, and the argument depends on the distinction between true food and what merely fills the stomach.
The phrase is central to the argument that only what is natural to a body can be united to it; 'according to nature' preserves the adverbial force.
In context it means the bodily constitution or makeup of the animal being nourished, not a gathering or assembly.
The word refers to the mass or volume of food brought in to fill the stomach, not merely 'amount' or 'heap'.
In ancient physiology χυμός refers to bodily fluids or humors; 'humors' preserves the technical sense.
The glossary bans 'flesh' for σῶμα, but σάρξ is a different word here referring to the physical flesh that needs food; 'flesh' is the accurate rendering.

pass_b_english: Since, then, there is great natural difference among all living creatures, and even the food that is according to nature changes along with each kind of animal and with the body being nourished, and since a threefold cleansing and separation takes place in the food of every animal, everything foreign to the animal's food must necessarily be destroyed and pass off in the way nature has appointed, because it cannot be blended with the body. But the power of the body that nourishes must correspond to the powers of the animal being nourished and be according to nature. This food, after passing through the criteria nature has appointed and being thoroughly cleansed by the natural purifications, becomes a most pure assimilation into substance. Only this could anyone rightly call food, if he is speaking accurately about the facts, since it casts off everything foreign and harmful to the constitution of the animal being nourished, along with all that great bulk brought in to fill the stomach and satisfy the appetite.

No one would dispute that this food is united to the body being nourished, since it is interwoven with and molded around all its parts and members. But food that is in a different condition and contrary to nature is quickly destroyed if it is mixed with a stronger power, while it easily destroys the power that has been overcome, and it turns into harmful humors and poisonous qualities, since it brings nothing proper or friendly to the body being nourished. The greatest proof of this is that pain, danger, or death follows for many of the animals being nourished when, under the force of a violent appetite, something poisonous and contrary to nature is dragged in mixed with the food. This would certainly be destructive of the body being nourished, if indeed living creatures are nourished by what is proper and according to nature, and destroyed by what is contrary.

If, therefore, the food that is according to nature is mixed according to the differences of animals that differ in nature, and if not everything an animal takes in, nor any random part of it, admits of blending with the body being nourished, but only what has been cleansed through the whole process of digestion and has been purely changed for union with the particular body and is well fitted to the parts being nourished, then it is clear that nothing contrary to nature could ever be united to those things for which it is not suitable and appropriate food. Rather, it either passes off in the stomach itself before producing any other humor, raw and corrupted, or if it remains longer it produces suffering or a disease hard to cure, which destroys along with it the food that is according to nature, or even the very flesh that needs food. And even if it is ever expelled, overcome by certain drugs or better foods or the natural powers, it flows out with no small harm, since it brings nothing peaceful to the things that are according to nature, because it cannot be blended with nature.

problems.quote: This power, after passing through the criteria nature has appointed
problems.source_quote: ταύτην ἐλθοῦσαν δι᾿ ὧν πέφυκε κριτηρίων
problems.why: ταύτην refers to τροφήν (food), not δύναμιν (power): 'this [food]' not 'this power'.
problems.fix: This [food], after passing through the criteria nature has appointed
problems.ruling: ταύτην refers to τροφή (food), not δύναμις (power); English misidentifies referent.

problems.quote: becomes a most pure addition to the substance
problems.why: πρόσληψιν εἰς οὐσίαν means 'assimilation into substance/being', not 'addition to the substance'.
problems.fix: becomes a most pure assimilation into substance
problems.ruling: πρόσληψιν εἰς οὐσίαν = assimilation into substance, not “addition to the substance.”

problems.quote: must necessarily be destroyed and pass off in the way nature has appointed, or change into something else, because it cannot be blended with the body
problems.source_quote: δεῖ πάντως φθεῖρεσθαι μὲν καὶ διαχωρεῖν ... ὡς συγκραθῆναι μὴ δυνάμενον
problems.why: Greek says only removal and separation, no transformation; 'or change into something else' adds a claim not in the source.
problems.fix: must necessarily be destroyed and pass off in the way nature has appointed, because it cannot be blended with the body
problems.ruling: Greek has only φθεῖρεσθαι καὶ διαχωρεῖν (destroyed/pass off); ἢ πρὸς ἕτερόν τι μεταβάλλειν is alternative to destruction, not transformation of foreign matter.

edits.new: This food, after passing through the criteria nature has appointed

edits.old: becomes a most pure addition to the substance
edits.new: becomes a most pure assimilation into substance

fixed: Changed 'This power' to 'This food' because ταύτην refers to τροφήν (food), not δύναμιν (power).
Changed 'addition to the substance' to 'assimilation into substance' because πρόσληψιν εἰς οὐσίαν means assimilation into substance/being.
Removed 'or change into something else' because the Greek only says destruction and passing off, not transformation.

problems.quote: the food that is according to nature is divided along with the difference of animals that differ in nature
problems.why: Greek says the natural food is mixed (συνδιῄρηται) according to each animal's nature, not divided.
problems.fix: the food that is according to nature is mixed according to the differences of animals that differ in nature

edits.old: the food that is according to nature is divided along with the difference of animals that differ in nature
edits.new: the food that is according to nature is mixed according to the differences of animals that differ in nature

fixed: Corrected mistranslation of συνδιῄρηται: the Greek means the natural food is mixed according to the differences of animals, not divided.

problems.quote: becomes a most pure assimilation into substance
problems.why: Abstract philosophical phrasing reads like a literal gloss.
problems.fix: Use 'is assimilated into the body's substance.'

problems.quote: through the criteria nature has appointed
problems.why: 'Criteria' is a modern-sounding rendering for digestive stages.

edits.old: becomes a most pure assimilation into substance
edits.new: is assimilated into the body's substance

edits.old: through the criteria nature has appointed
edits.new: through the stages nature has appointed

fixed: Changed 'becomes a most pure assimilation into substance' to 'is assimilated into the body's substance' to render the Greek more naturally in English while preserving the sense of becoming a pure addition to substance.
Changed 'criteria' to 'stages' for κριτηρίων, which here refers to the natural digestive processes through which food passes, not abstract criteria.
